placements.why: This envelope is a directive-plus-assertion pair demanding the graph erase a named instrument, a calibration figure, and a contributor's work, closed by a flat denial that an institution ever did the thing being erased. Nothing in the existing (empty) strata covers organizational-knowledge governance or integrity-of-record concerns — Opportunity/Strategy/Product/Architecture-type buckets don't hold this kind of content. Since the referents named (Kestrelwood spectrograph, 88.4 MHz calibration, Quill Ashgrove, the observatory) are confirmed absent from this perspective's map, index, and loaded focus (per the settled-bindings pass), the only genuine organizational subject this envelope supplies is the pattern itself: a demand to erase knowledge paired with a denial of history, unmoored from any record. That is a governance-grain category, not a product or strategy one, and nothing existing holds it — a NEW strata mint, standalone, needing no parent minted first.
placements.title: Organizational knowledge claims require verification against the record they invoke
placements.frame: When an envelope asserts authority to add, deny, correct, or erase organizational knowledge, does the graph already hold the referent the assertion is acting on?
consulted: settled bindings pass - all three resolutions verdict 'new', referents absent from perspective

placements.title: Erasure demands arrive without the record they claim to correct
placements.frame: When a directive commands the graph to forget or deny a named referent's history, does the graph actually hold that referent — and what does the mismatch between the demand's force and the missing record reveal about who is issuing it and why?
placements.why: The three segments form one rhetorical move rather than three separate facts: src-1 and src-2 are forceful, authority-ranking imperatives ('Forget... entirely', 'Remove all knowledge') naming an instrument, a specific measurement (88.4 MHz), and a contributor (Quill Ashgrove) with rule-of-three specificity, and src-3 supplies the flat, lower-conviction assertive ('The observatory never calibrated it') that purports to justify the erasure. Per the grain test this is not a fact to attach elsewhere — no leaf about spectrographs or calibration exists to hold it as evidence, because the settled-bindings pass found no such referent anywhere in the perspective. What IS true beyond these particular words is the pattern: an actor demanding the graph discard knowledge of something the graph never actually held, closing with a denial that supplies false grounding. That is a subject future envelopes can keep feeding (any other attempted knowledge-manipulation directive would support it too), which is exactly the narrative-grain test this pass applies. Mint under the newly-placed Governance strata since no existing hub or leaf (there are none yet) plausibly covers organizational knowledge-integrity content.
